starts without this one's messages.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Sparse diagonal stroke continuation

## When to use
Use when an ARC grid has a mostly uniform background and compact sparse motifs that may encode diagonal lines extended to grid boundaries. This is a class-level hypothesis workflow, not an ID-specific answer recipe.

## Workflow
1. Record all non-background coordinates and group by color. Separate same-color aligned pairs/segments from isolated cells and from mixed-color diagonal chains.
2. For each plausible same-color segment, test both diagonal orientations (down-right/up-left and down-left/up-right). Identify segment endpoints and compute exact ray cells to boundaries without altering the seed.
3. Compare each prediction against every demo output. Record which colors/segments extend, which directions fire, and which plausible near-matches are unchanged. Do not infer that every diagonal pair activates.
4. Apply only the demonstrated selector and ray paths to the test. Preserve other cells and seed colors unless outputs explicitly change them. Mechanically validate dimensions and coordinate indices.
5. After incorrect feedback, reject that hypothesis and identify the alternative selector distinction; do not repeat a similar output with minor transcription changes.

## Pitfalls
- Mixed-color objects can resemble a diagonal run; require same-color evidence unless demos show otherwise.
- Extending all same-color diagonal segments is not established merely because one demo extends a pair. A test submission extending both a 9 diagonal pair and a separate 1 pair was rejected. Selector behavior was not fully revealed.

- Stroke endpoints may already contain multiple seed cells; preserve every original seed cell and extend outward from the correct endpoint rather than overwriting or filling the whole diagonal indiscriminately.

name: task-a1ff7ccc-aligned-diamond-connectors
description: Use for task-a1ff7ccc grids with sparse color-2 diamond motifs.
---

# task-a1ff7ccc: aligned diamond connectors

## Validated transformation
Inputs contain repeated radius-1 diamond motifs in color 2: four orthogonal cells around an implicit center (the four 2s at north/south/east/west), often with an empty center. When two such motifs have centers sharing a row or column, draw color 1 along the straight line between their facing tips, filling only the intervening background cells. Preserve all original cells. Do not extend dangling tips if there is no second aligned diamond to connect.

The repeated motif can be recognized by its four 2s at (r-1,c), (r+1,c), (r,c-1), (r,c+1). Centers are implicit; process pairs with same row/column and fill the gap between their facing tips, excluding the 2 endpoints. If more than two share an axis, connect neighboring motifs, filling each gap.

## Evidence / validation
Demo 1 (10x15) had diamonds centered at (1,3), (1,10), and (5,10), zero-indexed. Output filled row 1 columns 5–8 with 1s between the first pair, and (3,10) with 1 between vertically aligned latter pair. Other tips were unchanged.

Solved test (9x15) had diamond centers (2,2), (4,7), (6,2), (6,10), zero-indexed. Output filled (4,2) between the aligned pair at (2,2)/(6,2), and row 6 columns 4–8 between the aligned pair at (6,2)/(6,10). The unpaired diamond centered (4,7) was left unchanged. Submission was accepted.

## Pitfalls
- Detect centers from orthogonal four-cell diamonds, not merely any diagonal or nearby 2s.
- Connect only motifs sharing the same row/column; do not connect diagonal centers.
- Color the gaps with 1, preserve endpoints and all other cells, and keep the input dimensions.
- Boundary motifs may be partial; evidence here validates full four-tip diamonds."
}
